visual_source_files.evidence: GitHub root asset (1024×363) reproduces the PDF Figure 2 token lanes, Patch Encoder, latent transformer, Patch Decoder, colors, and arrows; exact visual match by 200 dpi PDF inspection. It was read remotely into /tmp for comparison and not added to the repository.
Inspected source defines a scaling chart, but its model domain is BLT Space/SpaceByte/LLaMA/Megabyte++ and does not match the LST/Baseline HellaSwag curves in Figures 1 or 4.
Inspected config points to 4b_df.json, 500m_df.json, scaling_arch_df.json, and scaling_df.json; these data files were not present in the acquired compact source and do not bind the PDF chart values.
Inspected source creates an entropy line/rule chart, but no entropy figure appears in this 18-page PDF; it is not used as evidence for Figures 1–6.
Inspected config targets entropy_figure.pdf and score/threshold files; no corresponding paper object or acquired data file was found.
Inspected file contains only the repository copyright header and no visual parameters.

source_acquisition.search_note: The PDF explicitly links https://github.com/facebookresearch/lst and the OpenReview record is https://openreview.net/forum?id=krGpQzo8Mz. gh auth status and gh API confirm the exact repository title, README paper title, ICLR 2026 Oral claim, and default branch main. The automated reports/tables/visual_source_inventory.csv row says exact_visual_source and lists five acquired lst/plotting files; manual inspection finds the root lst-figure.jpg is an exact Figure 2 asset, while scaling_figures.py targets BLT/SpaceByte/LLaMA/Megabyte++ and entropy_figure.py targets an absent entropy chart. The repository tree contains no matching plot source/data for Figures 1, 4, or 6 and no Table 1–13 generator/TeX/export. Therefore visual-source coverage is partial: Figure 2 is source-exact and all remaining objects are audited from the PDF as the factual source.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Figures 1, 4, and 6 reuse a four-category blue/orange/green/red LST/Baseline × Speech/Text palette with Speech solid triangles and Text dashed x markers. Figure 2 uses pastel modality/module blocks; Figure 3 adds purple alignment markers; Figure 5 uses categorical word-cluster colors. Tables are black/white booktabs layouts with bold best values and no cell-color encoding. Color is paired with line, marker, label, or panel semantics but remains important for cross-series identity.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Figures 1, 2, 4, and 6 are predominantly vector text/paths; Figure 3 contains a 1678×852 raster illustration at about 697 dpi plus vector captions; Figure 5 contains three 2100×1800 raster panels at about 1193 dpi plus vector captions. Tables 1–13 are predominantly vector text and rules. The GitHub lst-figure.jpg is a separate exact source asset for Figure 2.
paper_style.style_consistency: Nimbus Roman No9 L and Computer Modern math recur in body, captions, tables, and formulae; Arial/DejaVu Sans form local chart/diagram systems. Booktabs tables share two-level task headers, bold best values, and thin horizontal rules. The four-series chart grammar is stable across main and appendix, while diagrams and t-SNE use local pastel/categorical palettes. Figure text is readable at the 200 dpi render but some internal labels are small and color identity is not fully grayscale-safe.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1: Comparison of LST and Baseline on HellaSwag story completion under two experimental setups, (a) compute-controlled: same number of training iterations and (b) data-controlled: same amount of training data.

color.semantic_mapping: LST Speech、LST Text、Baseline Speech、Baseline Text 分别以蓝/橙/绿/红表示；实线/虚线和三角/x marker 为 Speech/Text 的冗余提示。

encodings.x: Panel (a): total training iterations, 250k–500k; panel (b): total training tokens, 160B–330B.
encodings.y: HellaSwag accuracy (%) on a linear scale in both panels.
encodings.color: Four method/modality combinations: LST Speech, LST Text, Baseline Speech, Baseline Text.
encodings.shape: Triangle markers for Speech and x markers for Text; no shape difference for LST versus Baseline.
encodings.line: Solid Speech lines and dashed Text lines; light gray horizontal dashed grid.
encodings.facet: Compute-controlled fixed iterations versus data-controlled fixed data budget.
encodings.text: Panel subtitles, axis titles, four-item legends, and direct endpoint percentages.

figures.data_and_statistics: HellaSwag accuracy point estimates under two budget controls. The chart has no sample denominator, seed/run count, error bar, interval, or inferential test; exact headline changes such as +6.5 and +5.2 percentage points are supplied by Table 3 and the prose.
figures.evidence_relation: Information-density mismatch in the introduction → LST latent patching preview → two-control headline comparison → Tables 3–4 complete budget matrices → Figure 4 scaling → Table 6/Appendix ablations.
design_strengths: The compute and data controls are placed side by side with a common y metric.
The four series reuse a stable visual grammar that reappears in Figures 4 and 6.
Endpoint labels make the headline comparison readable without tracing every segment.
design_weaknesses: The caption does not define S→S/T→T, colors, or uncertainty.
LST versus Baseline remains color-dependent and is not fully grayscale-safe.
Sparse point estimates do not communicate run variability or benchmark denominators.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair compute-controlled and data-controlled panels with one shared series grammar, then bind the plotted endpoints to a table containing exact differences, denominators, and run definitions.

evidence.label: Figure 1 — PDF p.2 rendered at 200 dpi

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2: Latent Speech-Text Transformer (LST). The model encodes BPE text tokens and HuBERT speech tokens into a shared latent space. A Patch Encoder compresses local speech segments into patch representations, which are jointly processed with text tokens. A Patch Decoder predicts future speech tokens from latent representations, enabling alignment and transfer across modalities.

color.semantic_mapping: 浅绿 text、浅橙 speech、蓝色 encoder/decoder、浅绿中心 transformer、灰色 silence/latent grouping；标签、形状和虚线同时承担角色提示。

encodings.x: Left-to-right processing: modality tokens and HuBERT spans → Patch Encoder → shared latent transformer → Patch Decoder/output tokens.
encodings.y: Parallel text/speech lanes, silence and spoken-word groups; no numeric y scale.
encodings.color: Pastel blocks distinguish text, speech, silence, local patch modules, latent representation, and global transformer.
encodings.shape: Token rectangles, tall encoder/decoder boxes, rounded global-transformer container, dashed grouping boxes.
encodings.line: Solid arrows show data flow; dashed connectors and boundaries show correspondence/grouping.
encodings.facet: Input/encoding, shared latent processing, and decoding/output are sequential regions of one diagram.
encodings.text: Modality markers, s1–s7, spoken-word labels, Silence, HuBERT Tokens, and module names.

figures.data_and_statistics: Conceptual interface diagram with no sample count, denominator, aggregation, uncertainty, or plotted statistic. It establishes token→latent patch→token structure; Table 7 supplies module depth/dimension/head/window details.
figures.evidence_relation: Introduction information-density gap → Figure 2 shared-latent interface → Figure 3 boundary choices → Section 3 patch equations/schedule → Tables 6/7/13 and Figure 5 mechanism/efficiency evidence.
design_strengths: The modality lanes, local encoder, global transformer, and decoder form one readable flow.
Colors, labels, shape hierarchy, and dashed grouping jointly expose the interface.
The GitHub `lst-figure.jpg` asset matches the PDF token streams, blocks, labels, and arrows exactly.
design_weaknesses: Small token labels and connectors make the central flow dense at normal paper scale.
Causal masking, cross-attention, and 4→1 compression are not drawn explicitly.
The caption does not state the curriculum inference boundary or the local attention window.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a token→local compression→shared global model→local reconstruction architecture strip, paired with an appendix configuration table for dimensions and attention windows.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3: Illustrations of alignment and patching methods. (a) Static patching segments speech into fixed-size patches, while aligned patching uses Wav2Vec2+CTC boundaries. (sw = spoken word and sil = silence.) (b) Example of alignment from Wav2Vec2 + CTC, where purple markers indicate word boundaries, aligning the audio signal with corresponding text.

color.semantic_mapping: 左 panel 的 token/patch blocks 与 spoken-word/silence 标签区分 patch 规则；右 panel 紫色 marker 表示 CTC word boundaries。

encodings.x: Left: ordered speech/token spans; right: ordered word/audio alignment example without a measured time axis.
encodings.y: Rows for aligned versus static patching and an audio/word correspondence lane; no numeric y scale.
encodings.color: Patch block roles and purple boundary markers.
encodings.shape: Rectangular token spans, boundary lines/markers, and audio/spectrogram-like raster.
encodings.line: Segmentation boundaries and alignment markers; no quantitative line series.
encodings.facet: Panel (a) abstract static/aligned segmentation; panel (b) Wav2Vec2+CTC example.
encodings.text: Text transcript, spoken-word/silence labels, `sw`/`sil`, and subpanel captions.

figures.data_and_statistics: Illustrative token/audio segments rather than a sample statistic. There is no denominator, repeated run, uncertainty, or significance display; the visual explains the boundary semantics used by Tables 6 and 10 and Figure 5.
figures.evidence_relation: Speech/text boundary mismatch → Figure 2 patch interface → Figure 3 static versus forced alignment → Section 3.1 sets P_i and aligned ranges → Table 6/Table 10 boundary ablations and Figure 5 word-level representations.
design_strengths: Abstract segmentation and a concrete alignment example are paired in two panels.
Silence as a separately handled patch is visible and caption-defined.
The caption defines `sw`, `sil`, alignment source, and purple markers.
design_weaknesses: The audio panel has no time ticks, so boundary offset cannot be quantitatively checked.
Color and small labels lose clarity after grayscale or aggressive resizing.
Curriculum’s training-to-static-inference transition is absent from the figure and caption.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a rule-based token segmentation schematic with a real alignment snapshot, and define abbreviations, boundary source, silence handling, and any deployment-time dependency in the caption.

encodings.y: HellaSwag accuracy (%) on a linear scale.
encodings.color: LST/Baseline crossed with Speech/Text, matching Figures 1 and 6.
encodings.shape: Speech triangle versus Text x markers; line color separates LST and Baseline.
encodings.line: Solid Speech and dashed Text trajectories with light gray horizontal grid.

figures.evidence_relation: Figure 1 budget headline → Figure 4 scale and training dynamics → Table 8 1B/7B fixed-token check → Table 13 sequence/FLOPs proxy → data-limited and modality limitations.
design_strengths: The cross-scale endpoint and large-model trajectory answer different scaling questions in one figure.
The four-series grammar is stable across budget and ratio figures.
Subcaptions state the compute-optimal/sub-optimal distinction and critical token budgets.
design_weaknesses: The evidence covers one benchmark and point estimates without run variability.
Two panels use different x semantics, so the reader must rely on subcaptions.
Token-count efficiency remains a proxy; hardware wall-clock and end-to-end latency are absent.
figures.reusable_pattern: Combine a cross-scale endpoint panel with a matched-budget training trajectory, and state the optimality/data-limited regime alongside the plotted comparison.

color.semantic_mapping: 每个 panel 的点色表示词 identity/lexical cluster；panel 标题区分 personal pronouns、sharp tools、water terms。

encodings.x: Unlabeled t-SNE coordinate 1; no semantic numeric scale or tick labels.
encodings.y: Unlabeled t-SNE coordinate 2; no semantic numeric scale or tick labels.
encodings.color: Word identity within each lexical category.
encodings.shape: Colored scatter points; no additional marker-shape channel.
encodings.line: No connecting lines, reference lines, or grid.

The surrounding text reports within-word similarity ≈0.87, between-word similarity ≈0.43, and silhouette 0.65–0.68, but the raster panels show no sample count, t-SNE parameter, repeated embedding, or uncertainty.
figures.evidence_relation: Alignment should create semantically coherent word patches → Figure 5 three-category embedding clusters → similarity/silhouette summary → Table 6/Table 10 alignment and curriculum results → cross-modal alignment interpretation.
design_strengths: The three panels use one template and make cluster tightness visually comparable.
Same-word clusters and nearby related words turn the word-level-patch claim into a concrete diagnostic.
The caption identifies the model, HellaSwag speech source, grouping, and qualitative conclusion.
design_weaknesses: Unlabeled t-SNE axes obscure global distance and make stability hard to assess.
Point identity relies heavily on color and is weak in grayscale.
No sample count, perplexity, random seed, or repeated-embedding stability is shown.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a small qualitative scatter grid for mechanism diagnosis, but pair it with quantitative similarity/silhouette, sample counts, and embedding-stability checks.

figures.label: Figure 6

caption.text: Figure 6: Effect of speech-to-text token ratio at 200k iterations. Results are reported on HellaSwag under both S→S and T→T.

color.semantic_mapping: LST Speech、LST Text、Baseline Speech、Baseline Text 分别以蓝/橙/绿/红表示；实线/虚线和三角/x marker 为 Speech/Text 的冗余提示。

encodings.y: HellaSwag accuracy (%) on a linear scale.
encodings.color: LST/Baseline crossed with Speech/Text, shared with Figures 1 and 4.
encodings.shape: Speech triangles and Text x markers; Speech solid versus Text dashed.

figures.evidence_relation: Main text’s roughly one-third speech allocation → Figure 6 ratio ablation → Appendix A.6 macro-score peak at 1:2 and 1:1 text-side drop → Tables 3/4 budget conclusions.
design_strengths: The series show the speech gain/text cost trade-off on one reading path.
The main-paper four-series syntax remains stable in the appendix.
The 1:2 operating point and 1:1 text degradation are visually inspectable.
design_weaknesses: Connecting discrete ratios with lines suggests a continuous interpolation.
Macro score is discussed in prose but not plotted or labeled.
Ratio changes exposure and sequence composition together, so the visual does not isolate one mechanism.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: The sequence is information-density mismatch → token/patch architecture → static/aligned boundary mechanism → controlled-budget main comparison → scale/dynamics → ASR/TTS transfer → embedding diagnosis → patching ablation → appendix ratio, stability, data-version, low-level, and token-accounting checks.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Figure captions use title plus setup/interpretation; Figure 2–3 explain interfaces and Figure 4 subcaptions state the scaling finding. Figure 1 and Figure 6 omit series definitions and uncertainty. Table captions are short object/setup statements; Table 9 uniquely defines three runs and Ave/Std, while Table 13 spells out the accounting derivation.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Main result Tables 3–4 and ablation Tables 6/10 use two-level headers with task groups and S→S/T→T subcolumns. Table 5 groups ASR/TTS by Task and adds clean/other plus context/generation units. Appendix tables reuse the same direction and task grammar, with Table 9 adding Ave/Std subcolumns and Table 13 separating interleaved speech/text from text-only units.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 2 and Table 7 bind encoder/global-transformer/decoder interfaces to architecture details; Figure 3 and Tables 6/10 bind boundary semantics to ablations; Figures 1/4 and Tables 3/4/8 bind budgets and scale; Figure 5 supplies qualitative alignment diagnosis; Table 5 and Table 13 bind downstream units and cost accounting.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: The main paper keeps headline budget comparisons, scale, downstream quality, and the primary patching table. Appendix A.4–A.11 adds fixed-token endpoints, three-run stability, speech ratio, BPE alignment, TTS version robustness, low-level capability, sequence accounting, and aligner perturbation; these complete boundaries but do not add wall-clock measurement.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Caption PDF objects are Nimbus Roman No9 L at approximately 9.963 pt; table and body text use Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern, with Arial/DejaVu Sans in chart/diagram internals. Weight and rule treatment are stable, while local plot labels are smaller than captions.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: The chart palette and Speech/Text line/marker convention recur across Figures 1/4/6. Figure 2–3 and Figure 5 use separate local semantic palettes; labels and shapes provide some redundancy, but four-series and word-cluster identities still degrade in grayscale.

most_reusable_patterns: Token→patch→shared-global→token architecture strip with an appendix module-configuration table.
Four-series budget/scale/ratio line grammar reused across controlled comparisons and ablations.
Model × budget × task × S→S/T→T tables that bind performance to a cost proxy.
Ave/Std two-level stability table and explicit token-accounting table for uncertainty and efficiency boundaries.
Abstract segmentation plus concrete forced-alignment example for mechanism explanation.
failure_patterns: Main quantitative objects are mostly single point estimates; repeat/Std evidence is deferred to Table 9 and denominators remain absent.
Token/sequence savings are proxies without wall-clock or end-to-end latency.
Approximately matched patch sizes confound boundary semantics and compute in Tables 6 and 10.
Figure 5 t-SNE is qualitative and under-specified for stability or global distance.
Color remains a major identity channel despite partial line/marker/text redundancy.
TTS other CER is worse for LST than baseline, limiting a blanket no-quality-cost claim.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: Use a shared token/patch mechanism diagram and four-series budget/scale lines for the headline, bind effect and proxy cost in S→S/T→T tables, and move alignment, stability, data-version, low-level, and accounting checks to the appendix for explicit boundary control.
